key_insight: Longer on-policy distillation trajectories yield diminishing supervision returns, while randomly varying rollout horizons can preserve learning from deeper response states at lower cost.
engineering_relevance: Batch-shared stochastic horizons reduce per-update compute while retaining efficient parallel generation without per-sequence horizon scheduling.
method: Analyze supervision utility, cross-position transfer, and gradient structure across response depths.
Randomly sample one shared rollout horizon per training batch to reduce redundant supervision.
Characterize horizon-induced reweighting bias and derive a compute–reweighting trade-off.
evidence_signal: Experiments report slightly higher mathematical reasoning accuracy at approximately 45% of standard OPD's per-update cost, with competitive code generation performance at around 60% of baseline cost.
watch_item: Random horizons reweight supervision across response depths; lower per-update cost does not by itself establish lower total training cost.
paper_title: Rethinking Supervision Scaling in On-Policy Distillation: From Dense Supervision to Stochastic Horizons
